findings.message:
Freshness is decided by review timestamp vs. commit timestamp instead of the reviewed commit SHA: `return latestCopilotReview.After(lastCommitDate), nil` treats a review as fresh whenever its `submitted_at` is later than the head commit's `committer.date`, without checking which commit the review actually covers. The PR description states the check should compare each Copilot review's `commit_id` against the current PR head SHA, which this implementation does not do. Commit timestamps are also not reliable ordering evidence: `git rebase --committer-date-is-author-date`, `GIT_COMMITTER_DATE`, or imported/cherry-picked patches can give the current head commit a `committer.date` older than a review that was submitted for a previous commit.
Scenario: Copilot starts reviewing commit A; while it is running, the developer pushes commit B (committer date 10:00); Copilot then submits its review of commit A at 10:05. `latestCopilotReview` (10:05) is after `lastCommitDate` (10:00), so the function reports fresh and cmd/root.go exits early: commit B is never reviewed even though Copilot's review only covered A.
Read the PR head SHA (`GET repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{n}` -> `head.sha`) and compare it to the `commit_id` field of the Copilot reviews, e.g. return fresh only when some Copilot review has `commit_id == headSHA`; keep the timestamp only as a fallback when `commit_id` is empty.
